caveats: 'early-type'/'late-type' come from Gillessen 2009/2017. They are a published class (Br-gamma vs CO bandheads), not an MK type. MK types exist only for S38 (G7.5III), S83 (O9-9.5 V), S87 (OB I?), S96 and S97 (Ofpe/WN9).
S39 and S55: Gillessen 2017 says the spectral type is unknown; no later paper found assigns one, so null.
Paumard 2006 lists S66 (E17) and S67 (E15) with SpType '?'. They are early-type with no subtype.

Cross-IDs to Paumard E-numbers come from Gillessen 2009 Sect. 7.3.1, which names them (S66=E17, S67=E15/S1-3, S83=E16/S0-15, S87=E21, S96=E20/IRS16C, S97=E23/IRS16SW). Bartko 2009 VizieR rows carry no names; I matched them by position and K only to note RV agreement.
R44 = UCLA S2-21 rests on von Fellenberg 2022 Table 4. R34 and S91 have no cross-ID in any table opened.

RVs are single-epoch line-of-sight velocities as tabulated (LSR-corrected per the source papers). For short-period stars (S38, S54, S55) they vary strongly along the orbit; Gillessen 2017 Table 5 holds multi-epoch series for those three.
S83 RVs disagree beyond their errors: Paumard 2006 -424+-70, Gillessen 2009 -557+-26, Yelda 2014 -597+-8.
Masses for S67 and R44 (Feldmeier-Krause 2015) come from isochrones, not dynamics. The S97 mass (~50 Msun per component) is an approximate binary estimate with no formal error.

No individual Teff found for any star except S96 (Martins 2007). Habibi 2019 gives only a group range for S38's class. Martins 2006's 28000 K for IRS16SW is an assumed light-curve input, not a measurement, so it is excluded.
Gillessen 2009 Sect. 6.1 says RVs were measured for S85 and S89, but its Appendix B table has no v_z row for them, so they are null.
SIMBAD's own RV/sp_type fields (e.g. S83 RV -597 from Yelda 2014) are aggregations. Values here were taken from the papers or VizieR tables directly.
